chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Rupert Cole, Bob Carroll and Elmer Williams
summary: He briefly characterizes Cole and Carroll and calls Elmer Williams, long with Chick Webb, the most melodic tenor he heard.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Rupert Cole was a good melodic alto player and Bob Carroll was a very good tenor player. Bob Carroll liked Coleman Hawkins, so you know how he played.
I can go back in the early thirties -- Elmer
Williams was the most melodic tenor player I ever heard.
He was with Chick Webb for years and years and years and he -- he didn't leave Chick until -- when Ben Webster left Fletcher --
Elmer went out, he went there with Fletcher about 1935, '36 when Fletcher had that band in the Grand Terrace.
Elmer Williams left Chick to go out there to play with him.
